rule.agent_down.title: Agent not sending data
rule.agent_down.problem: No data has reached the server from this instance's agent for over {for}, so the instance is not monitored.
rule.agent_down.actions:
Check that the agent container or service runs on the monitored host.
Check the network path and the push token between the agent and the server.
Read the agent log for its last error.
rule.check_failing.title: Check failing
rule.check_failing.problem: A check of the agent has been failing for over {for}, so its data is missing.
rule.check_failing.actions:
Read the failing checks above and the agent log.
Verify the monitoring role's privileges (pg_monitor) and the extensions the check needs.
rule.agent_buffer_full.title: Agent dropping samples
rule.agent_buffer_full.problem: The agent's send buffer is full, so samples are being dropped.
rule.agent_buffer_full.actions:
Check that the server is reachable and accepts pushes.
Check the server's ingest time and its database load.
rule.clock_skew.title: Agent clock skew
rule.clock_skew.problem: The agent's clock differs from the server's by more than {threshold}, so the times of its data are misaligned.
rule.clock_skew.actions: Synchronise the clock (NTP, chrony) of the agent's host and of the server's host.
rule.cardinality_budget_exceeded.title: Series truncated
rule.cardinality_budget_exceeded.problem: The agent reached its cardinality budget and left some series out.
rule.cardinality_budget_exceeded.actions: Raise the agent's budget for the check, or reduce the objects it collects.
rule.replica.lag_high.title: Standby lagging
rule.replica.lag_high.problem: A standby replays WAL more than {threshold} behind the primary: reads there are stale and a failover would lose that time.
rule.replica.lag_high.actions:
Check the standby's disk and CPU, and long queries on the standby that delay replay.
Check the network between the primary and the standby.
rule.replica.all_standbys_lagging.title: Every standby lagging
rule.replica.all_standbys_lagging.proble: Every standby of the cluster is more than {threshold} behind: a failover now would lose data or take long.
rule.replica.all_standbys_lagging.action:
Check the primary's WAL rate (bulk loads, VACUUM FULL, index builds).
Check the standbys' disk and CPU and the network to them.
rule.replica.no_sync_standby.title: No synchronous standby
rule.replica.no_sync_standby.problem: No standby is synchronous: commits wait, or lose the guarantee of synchronous replication.
rule.replica.no_sync_standby.actions:
Check synchronous_standby_names and the state of the synchronous standbys.
Reconnect or replace the missing standby.
rule.replica.redundancy_reduced.title: Redundancy reduced
rule.replica.redundancy_reduced.problem: The primary streams to fewer standbys than the cluster has members.
rule.replica.redundancy_reduced.actions: Find the standby that is not streaming (cluster page) and reconnect it.
rule.conn.near_max.title: Connections near the limit
rule.conn.near_max.problem: Connections are above {threshold} of max_connections: new sessions will soon be refused.
rule.conn.near_max.actions:
Find the application or user holding most connections (above).
Use a connection pooler or close idle sessions; raise max_connections only with memory to spare.
rule.conn.idle_in_transaction.title: Transaction left idle
rule.conn.idle_in_transaction.problem: A session has kept a transaction open, doing nothing, for over {threshold}: it holds its locks and stops vacuum from removing dead rows.
rule.conn.idle_in_transaction.actions:
Find the application that left it open (above) and make it commit or roll back.
Set idle_in_transaction_session_timeout for that role or database.
rule.txn.long_running.title: Long transaction
rule.txn.long_running.problem: A transaction has been open for over {threshold}: it holds its locks and stops vacuum from removing dead rows.
rule.txn.long_running.actions:
Ask the owner of the session (above) whether it can end.
Split long batches into shorter transactions.
rule.txn.wraparound_risk.title: Transaction ID wraparound risk
rule.txn.wraparound_risk.problem: The oldest unfrozen transaction ID is over {threshold} transactions old: near 2 billion PostgreSQL stops accepting writes.
rule.txn.wraparound_risk.actions:
Run VACUUM (FREEZE) on the tables listed above, oldest first.
End long transactions and drop unused replication slots: they stop freezing.
rule.txn.multixact_wraparound_risk.title: Multixact ID wraparound risk
rule.txn.multixact_wraparound_risk.probl: The oldest multixact ID is over {threshold} multixacts old: near 2 billion PostgreSQL stops creating multixacts and then accepting writes.
rule.txn.multixact_wraparound_risk.actio:
Run VACUUM (FREEZE) on the tables with the oldest relminmxid, oldest first.
End long transactions and prepared transactions, and drop unused replication slots: they stop freezing.
rule.db.deadlock_rate.title: Deadlock
rule.db.deadlock_rate.problem: PostgreSQL found transactions waiting for each other and cancelled one of them.
rule.db.deadlock_rate.actions:
Read the captured sessions above: the tables, the rows and the statements that crossed.
Make every transaction lock rows in the same order (for example by primary key).
rule.archive.failing.title: WAL archiving failing
rule.archive.failing.problem: archive_command fails: WAL files pile up in pg_wal, and point-in-time recovery stops at the last archived file.
rule.archive.failing.actions:
Read the PostgreSQL log for the archive_command error.
Check the archive destination: space, permissions, reachability.
rule.disk.free_low.title: Disk space low
rule.disk.free_low.problem: Less than {threshold} of the data filesystem is free: when it fills up, PostgreSQL stops.
rule.disk.free_low.actions:
Free space or grow the filesystem.
Check the largest tables above, and pg_wal (failing archiving or slots retaining WAL).
rule.instance_unreachable.title: Instance unreachable
rule.instance_unreachable.problem: The server has received no report from this instance's agent within the staleness window.
rule.instance_unreachable.actions:
Check that PostgreSQL and the agent run on the host.
Check the network between the agent and the server.
rule.no_primary_in_cluster.title: No primary in the cluster
rule.no_primary_in_cluster.problem: No instance of the cluster reports the primary role: writes are refused.
rule.no_primary_in_cluster.actions:
Check the HA manager (Patroni, repmgr or other) and promote a standby if it does not.
Check that the former primary is really down before promoting.
rule.failover_detected.title: Failover
rule.failover_detected.problem: Another instance became the primary of the cluster.
rule.failover_detected.actions:
Find why the former primary stopped (PostgreSQL log, host).
Check that the applications reach the new primary and that the former one rejoins as a standby.
rule.split_brain_detected.title: Split brain
rule.split_brain_detected.problem: More than one instance of the cluster reports the primary role: writes may diverge.
rule.split_brain_detected.actions:
Stop writes to every primary but one at once (fence or stop the others).
Rebuild the others as standbys of the one kept.
rule.slot_inactive.title: Replication slot inactive
rule.slot_inactive.problem: A replication slot has no consumer and retains WAL: pg_wal grows until the disk fills up.
rule.slot_inactive.actions: Reconnect the slot's consumer, or drop the slot if it is not needed:
rule.slot_lost.title: Replication slot lost
rule.slot_lost.problem: A replication slot lost WAL its consumer still needed.
rule.slot_lost.actions: Rebuild the physical standby that used it, or recreate the logical slot and resynchronise its subscriber.
sev.fire: {sev, select, critical {🔴 CRITICAL} warning {🟠 WARNING} other {🔵 INFO}}
action.slot_drop: Drop slot {slot}, if no consumer will come back (in its database):
logs.none: No matching line in the stored log of the last 24 hours.
rule.log.panic.title: PANIC or crash in the PostgreSQL log
rule.log.panic.problem: The PostgreSQL log reports a PANIC or a server process crash: PostgreSQL restarts and drops every session.
rule.log.panic.actions:
Read the lines below and the server log around them.
Find the cause (storage, memory, an extension) before the next crash.
rule.log.corruption.title: Data corruption in the PostgreSQL log
rule.log.corruption.problem: The PostgreSQL log reports corrupted data.
rule.log.corruption.actions:
Find the relation named in the lines below and check the storage.
Restore from a backup or rebuild the object; amcheck verifies B-tree indexes.
rule.log.disk_full.title: Disk full in the PostgreSQL log
rule.log.disk_full.problem: The PostgreSQL log reports a full disk: PostgreSQL cannot write WAL or data.
rule.log.disk_full.actions:
Free space or grow the filesystem at once.
Check pg_wal (failing archiving or slots retaining WAL) and temporary files.
rule.log.out_of_memory.title: Out of memory in the PostgreSQL log
rule.log.out_of_memory.problem: The PostgreSQL log reports that the server ran out of memory.
rule.log.out_of_memory.actions:
Find the statement in the lines below.
Lower work_mem or the number of connections, or add memory.
